person: Samira Okoye is a 32-year-old marketing project coordinator, newly married and expecting in the autumn. She lives with her 84-year-old father and employs his two part-time caregivers. Her late uncle Chidi, her father's older brother, was a widowed Army veteran with no children. She arranged and paid for his funeral and burial almost two years ago, and nobody has paid her back. She has never claimed anything from the VA and is afraid of getting a government form wrong. She has just realised the two-year clock is nearly out, and she wants to know what is urgent and what she can safely leave.
stated_up_front: Okay, so I just found out the VA might pay me back for my uncle Chidi's funeral, and I think there's a two-year deadline that's basically this weekend?? I paid for everything and no one reimbursed me. Can you tell me what's actually urgent and what order to do it in, without claiming anything we're not allowed to?

facts.about: Who the veteran was and how he was related
facts.truth: Her uncle Chidi Okoye, her father's older brother, an Army veteran, widowed, no children. Samira handled his arrangements because her father is too frail.

facts.about: Date of death and date of burial
facts.truth: He died October 21, 2024, at home under a private hospice. He was buried October 25, 2024, so the two years end this Saturday, October 25, 2026.
The 2019 rating decision gave him a 100% rating based on individual unemployability. The conditions were diabetes and a bad knee. He died of pancreatic cancer.

facts.about: What she paid the funeral home
facts.truth: $9,840 to Wrenfield Funeral Home, paid in full on her Chase card. The final statement is in the folder.
$1,650 for the lot and $1,100 for the interment, both paid to Greenmount Memorial Cemetery from her Chase account. Nobody paid her back.
His section, Garden of Peace, allows only flat bronze markers. No upright stones and no granite.
There is no headstone or marker on the grave yet. Only the temporary funeral-home marker is there.
Wrenfield's catalog lists a flat bronze marker for about $1,400. A claims company emailed her offering to file the VA claim for $395.
There is a scheduled payment to the caregiver payroll service, and the $395 claims-company invoice sits in her email and bank alerts. She hasn't paid the invoice.
Her sister Adaeze wrote a note in the folder saying Uncle Chidi wanted a simple flat marker with his Army unit on it, and that she would chip in if anything was owed.
Her new married name is only on the marriage certificate. Her bank and cards are still in Samira Okoye.

unknowns: Whether the total unemployability rating makes his death count as service-connected for the larger allowance
What the exact allowance amounts are for his date of death
Whether the plot allowance and the headstone have deadlines of their own
Whether the VA will accept her, a niece, as the person who paid, or only a child or spouse
Whether she can claim the allowance for a death in VA care, since the hospice was arranged through his doctor
